title: Day 3: Cyber Security + Banking IT & Regulations
answer_format: answer is the option letter a–e mapping to options[0]–options[4]

questions.question: Which of the following is the standard used for digital certificates in a public key infrastructure?
questions.explanation: X.509 is the certificate format. SHA-256 = hash, RSA = asymmetric algorithm, AES = symmetric.

questions.question: In asymmetric encryption, which key is used to encrypt a message so that only the intended receiver can read it?
questions.explanation: Confidentiality: encrypt with the receiver's public key; only the receiver's private key can decrypt.

questions.question: Which of the following is mainly used to provide non-repudiation?
questions.explanation: A digital signature means the sender can't deny sending the message.

questions.question: What is the effective key length used by DES, excluding parity bits?
questions.explanation: DES key = 64 bits, of which 8 are parity, so 56 effective.

questions.question: Which of the following algorithms uses the same key for both encryption and decryption?
questions.explanation: AES is symmetric. RSA/ECDSA/DH are asymmetric; SHA-256 is a hash.

questions.question: How does salting improve the security of stored password hashes?
options: It converts plaintext to hashed text using MD5 without adding anything
It encrypts the hash using a symmetric algorithm
It stores the hash without any change
It compresses the hash to save storage
It adds a random value to the input before hashing, so every hash is unique
questions.explanation: A salt is a random value added before hashing; it defeats rainbow tables.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a property of a cryptographic hash function?
options: It can be reversed to recover the original input
The same input always gives the same output
questions.explanation: Hashes are one-way; they can't be reversed.

questions.question: In the CIA triad, ensuring that data is not altered without detection is called:
A digital signature is created by encrypting the message hash with:
questions.explanation: Sign with your own private key; others verify with your public key.

questions.question: How many keys are needed for 10 users to communicate privately in pairs using symmetric encryption?
What is the effective key length of DES?
The Diffie-Hellman algorithm is mainly used for:
options: Securely exchanging a shared secret key
questions.explanation: DH is for key exchange only.

questions.question: Which of the following is an asymmetric encryption algorithm?
questions.explanation: Asymmetric = RSA, ECC, DH, DSA. The rest are symmetric.

questions.question: Which security service does a digital signature NOT provide?
questions.explanation: Signatures don't encrypt the message, so no confidentiality.

questions.question: Which entity issues and signs digital certificates?
questions.explanation: The CA issues and signs certificates.

questions.question: Hiding a secret message inside an image file, so that nobody even knows the message exists, is called:
questions.explanation: Steganography hides the existence of a message; cryptography makes it unreadable.

questions.question: Verifying the identity of a user, for example through a password or OTP, is called:
questions.explanation: Authentication = who you are. Authorization = what you can do.

questions.question: A DDoS attack mainly targets which goal of the CIA triad?
What is the size of an MD5 hash?
After the TLS handshake is complete, the actual data is encrypted using:
options: A symmetric session key (such as AES)
questions.explanation: Hybrid encryption: asymmetric for key exchange, symmetric (AES) for data.

questions.question: DES uses a 64-bit key. How many of those bits are actually used for encryption?
Which group contains only asymmetric algorithms?
questions.explanation: RSA, ECC and DH are all asymmetric.

questions.question: What is the output size of the MD5 hash function?
How many keys are needed in total for 10 users to communicate using asymmetric encryption?
questions.explanation: Asymmetric: 2n = 20 (one key pair per user). 45 is the symmetric formula.

questions.question: HMAC provides which security services?
questions.explanation: HMAC = hash + secret key: integrity and authentication.

questions.question: Which mechanism is used to check whether a digital certificate has been revoked before its expiry date?
questions.explanation: CRL/OCSP check revocation. X.509 is just the format.

questions.question: What is the output size of SHA-256?
questions.explanation: The name gives it away: 256 bits.

questions.question: Which of the following is a symmetric stream cipher?
questions.explanation: RC4 is a stream cipher. AES/DES are block ciphers.

questions.question: In hybrid encryption, as used by HTTPS/TLS:
options: Only asymmetric encryption is used for all data
Symmetric encryption is used to exchange keys, and asymmetric encryption is used for the data
Asymmetric encryption (or Diffie-Hellman) is used to exchange a session key, and symmetric encryption is used for the data
questions.explanation: Asymmetric for the key exchange, then fast symmetric for the data.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: A hash can be reversed using the private key
Encryption can be reversed using the correct key
A salt makes identical passwords produce different hashes
questions.explanation: Hashes can't be reversed by any key.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes a watering hole attack?
options: Infecting a user's system through email attachments
Redirecting traffic from secure websites to fake login pages
Infecting a commonly visited website to target a specific group of users
Sending mass phishing emails to unknown users
Encrypting files and demanding a ransom
questions.explanation: Watering hole: infect the site the target group visits (PYQ 2025).

questions.question: Which of the following techniques helps prevent SQL injection attacks?
options: Running SQL queries in a loop
Giving admin rights to all users
questions.explanation: Input validation/sanitization and parameterized queries prevent SQLi (PYQ 2025).

questions.question: Which web application attack involves injecting malicious scripts into a trusted website to target its users?
questions.explanation: XSS injects scripts that run in other users' browsers (PYQ 2022).

questions.question: Which attack causes a logged-in user's browser to send unauthorised requests to a trusted web application without the user's consent?
questions.explanation: CSRF forges requests from a logged-in user's browser (PYQ 2024).

questions.question: Which type of DDoS attack sends spoofed ICMP echo requests to broadcast addresses, causing many systems to flood the victim with ICMP replies?
questions.explanation: Smurf = ICMP to broadcast with the victim's IP spoofed (PYQ 2023).

questions.question: What is the name of the attack in which an attacker overwhelms a web server by sending a very large number of HTTP requests?
A rogue wireless access point that closely imitates a legitimate Wi-Fi network to trick users and capture their credentials is an example of which attack?
Which form of snooping attack involves unauthorised monitoring of network communications to capture sensitive information?
Which type of malware replicates itself across a network without needing a host file or user action?
questions.explanation: Worm travels alone; a virus needs a host.

Which of the following is an example of a passive attack?
questions.explanation: Passive attacks only observe; eavesdropping is the classic one.

questions.question: A network of compromised computers, controlled by an attacker through a C&C server and often used to launch DDoS attacks, is called a:
Which type of Intrusion Detection System analyses network traffic in real time?
Which security approach permits only predefined, approved inputs or entities and rejects all others by default?
questions.explanation: Whitelisting = guest list; only approved entries get in (PYQ 2024).

questions.question: Which of the following threats is least effectively controlled by a traditional hardware firewall?
options: Data theft by authorised internal users
questions.explanation: Insiders' traffic is allowed by the rules (PYQ 2024).

questions.question: Which firewall monitors the state of every connection and allows or blocks packets based on that context, providing stronger security?

Match the access control models with their features. Models: A. Zero Trust, B. DAC, C. MAC, D. RBAC. Features: 1. Based on roles in an organisation, 2. Based on security labels/classification, 3. Access decided by the data owner, 4. Never trust, always verify (assume breach).
questions.explanation: Zero Trust = never trust; DAC = owner; MAC = labels; RBAC = roles (PYQ 2025).

questions.question: Which authorisation framework is commonly used in modern web applications to enable token-based access, and is often integrated into Single Sign-On systems?
In the Cyber Kill Chain, which phase combines a malicious payload with a specific exploit to prepare for delivery?
What is the main purpose of a DMZ?
options: To host public-facing servers in a separate zone from the internal network

questions.question: In server security, which of the following practices is NOT desirable?
options: Using a reverse proxy to hide server IP addresses
Deploying public-facing servers in a DMZ
Allowing unrestricted root login via SSH for faster access
questions.explanation: Unrestricted root SSH is a major risk (PYQ 2022).

questions.question: Which of the following is a true example of multi-factor authentication?
options: Password + OTP sent to the registered phone
questions.explanation: MFA needs different factor types: know + have. Password + PIN are both 'know'.

questions.question: Which approach is considered more secure because it rejects everything by default and allows only approved items?
Which of the following is commonly used to block or allow network ports such as HTTP and SSH?
What is the key difference between an IDS and an IPS?
options: An IDS blocks attacks, while an IPS only alerts
An IDS works only on hosts
An IPS sits inline and can actively block attacks, while an IDS only detects and alerts

questions.question: What is the main limitation of signature-based intrusion detection?
options: It produces too many false positives
It works only on wireless networks
questions.explanation: Signatures only match known attacks. Anomaly-based has more false positives.

questions.question: What is BitLocker?
options: A disk encryption feature in Windows

questions.question: A network is divided into smaller segments to isolate different groups of systems and control communication between them. What is the major benefit of network segmentation?
options: It removes the need for authentication
It reduces the impact of security breaches
It increases the number of security vulnerabilities
It allows unrestricted communication between all devices
It removes the need for network monitoring

questions.question: In banking, what is the primary role of KYC?
options: Verifying customer identity to prevent financial threats
Assessing customer income to decide credit eligibility
Monitoring account activity to improve transaction speed
Collecting customer data to personalise banking services
Evaluating customer records to recommend investments
questions.explanation: KYC = identity verification to prevent money laundering and fraud (PYQ Prelims 2026).

questions.question: In disaster recovery planning, which term refers to the maximum acceptable data loss, measured in time?
questions.explanation: RPO = data loss (Point in time). RTO = outage time (PYQ 2025).

questions.question: In business continuity planning, a Disaster Recovery Plan is part of which international standard?
Which statement about offsite recovery strategies is correct?
options: A cold site has all necessary equipment pre-installed and ready to use
A warm site is identical to a hot site, but without real-time data synchronisation
A hot site provides fully operational systems with real-time data mirroring and needs minimal downtime during recovery
A backup site is always fully equipped for immediate switchover
questions.explanation: Hot site = fully operational + real-time mirroring (PYQ 2022).

questions.question: An incremental backup copies:

Only the changes made since the last full backup
